searchText: You are greatly hurting readability by using t8n, t9n, and b11r instead of whatever the actual words are. And you are only saving typing 7-9 characters, which is almost never going to be worth it. Plus `t8n` is already a defined term in the internationalization (`i18n`) space 😛 > Who knew that replacing all of the letters in a word with a number would cause collisions! W1o k2w t2t r5eing a1l o0f t1e l4rs i0n a-1 w2d w2h aNaN n4r w3d c3e c7ns! I would further contend that it actually slows down typing in many cases because typing numbers is significantly harder for an experienced typist than typing letters/words. Pls don’t shoot the messenger 🤣 Ok I was reading all this with amusement, but now when I checkout <@543900561460822016>'s branch to start testing I'm faced with the following log message from the tip of the branch ``` cmd/evm: support withdrawals in t8n and b11r ``` what the hell is this? heh - it's the "transition (t8n) tool" and the "block builder (b11r) tool" they're used to fill the cross client tests run in hive If we're standardizing things, might I suggest: ``` build-tx build-blk transition ``` or hell, maybe even: ``` mktx mkblk ``` if we want to be even shorter. I don't think the issue is lack of brevity No, but `mktx` remains brief while being _way_ more obvious (though still opaque...)
